text:
Bitcoin remained trapped in a volatile $63,000–$64,000 consolidation zone late June 21, weighed down by historic institutional capital flight. The Crypto Fear and Greed Index lingers near 20 as U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs extended their withdrawal streak to six consecutive weeks, posting a massive $6.35 billion 30-day net outflow. Concurrently, miner capitulation metrics suggest a potential cycle floor may be forming near $59,000.

Regulatory scrutiny over digital asset infrastructure is severely intensifying. A coalition of five U.S. federal agencies proposed classifying Permitted Payment Stablecoin Issuers as financial institutions under the Bank Secrecy Act, mandating strict bank-grade AML compliance.

This structural crypto weakness is fundamentally tethered to a hawkish repricing of Federal Reserve policy under Chair Kevin Warsh. With the 2-year Treasury yield surging to its highest level since 2022 and the DXY hitting a one-year peak, risk-free rate differentials are aggressively siphoning liquidity. Until these elevated short-end sovereign yields retrace or the dollar demonstrably softens, non-yielding digital assets will continue struggling against traditional fixed-income alternatives.
